messages.subject: rstan installation, 'stan/lang/ast_def.cpp' file not found
parts:
I'm having trouble installing rstan, probably a problem with my configuration but... I can't configure it out.  The key session output lines seem to be:

/usr/local/Cellar/r/3.3.1/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/bin/R: line 193: /usr/local/Library/ENV/4.3/sed: No such file or directory

as well as

/usr/local/Cellar/r/3.3.1/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/bin/R: line 193: /usr/local/Library/ENV/4.3/sed: No such file or directory


ERROR: option '-e' requires a non-empty argument


clang: warning: optimization flag '-ffat-lto-objects' is not supported


lang__ast_def.cpp:18:10: fatal error: 'stan/lang/ast_def.cpp' file not found


#include <stan/lang/ast_def.cpp>


         ^


1 error generated.


make: *** [lang__ast_def.o] Error 1


ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘rstan’


* removing ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/rstan’



I can't figure out why the install script is calling sed (maybe this is common?) but it makes it hard to figure out.  If the issues is just R expecting to be able to call sed and not figuring it out I think it's a brew issue and I'll work on that but I can't see how that would make it hard for R to find the stan file. Anyway, any suggestions about how to investigate further would be helpful.

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: rstan installation, 'stan/lang/ast_def.cpp' file not found
parts:
On Tuesday, July 19, 2016 at 10:28:52 PM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Tuesday, July 19, 2016 at 9:54:05 PM UTC-4, Krzysztof Sakrejda wrote:
Should have said I do have it installed but that path is wrong... but I'm stuck at why it wants sed. Maybe I should just supply a symlink and be done with it. Brew's path machinations might not be playing nice with R's build scripts.  

Does installing another package with compiled code work? The rstan package does not actually use sed anywhere.

Yes it does, but it turns out that sed gets called in the script that parses R command lines arguments prior to calling the binary, so on my install, this script:

/usr/local/Cellar/r/3.3.1/R.framework/Versions/3.3/Resources/bin/R


was calling sed at

which, as indicated, does not exist.  I edited it to point at the os x vanilla /usr/bin/sed and rstan installs fine now... looks from Google as though the issue might just be a broken brew install script but a similar issue comes up with a broken libtool install script (that brew must rely on somewhere?) and one of the libtool config files on my laptop also contains that (non-existent) path so... I don't know.  I'll see how long the fix of editing the R startup script holds.  Thanks!

Krzysztof

 
Ben
